name: Ebed-melech
source_summary: An Ethiopian (Cushite) official in Zedekiah's court who rescued the prophet Jeremiah from a muddy cistern where officials had left him to die, and was promised his life would be spared when Jerusalem fell.
family_friendly_summary: Ebed-Melech was a Cushite official who worked in the king's palace in Jerusalem. When Judah's officials, angry at Jeremiah's warnings, threw the prophet into a deep, muddy cistern to die, Ebed-Melech acted with real courage. He went straight to King Zedekiah and pleaded for Jeremiah's life, then organized men and supplies -- old rags to cushion the ropes -- to carefully pull Jeremiah safely back out of the cistern. Because of his brave compassion for God's prophet, God later gave Ebed-Melech a special promise through Jeremiah: even though disaster was coming to Jerusalem, Ebed-Melech's own life would be protected because he had trusted God.
adult_story: Ebed-Melech, a Cushite (Ethiopian) eunuch serving in King Zedekiah's palace, heard that Judah's officials, furious at Jeremiah's prophecies urging surrender to Babylon, had thrown the prophet into an empty cistern to die in its mud, since striking him directly might have seemed too openly violent (Jeremiah 38:4-6). Ebed-Melech went immediately to Zedekiah, who was sitting at the Benjamin Gate, and pleaded on Jeremiah's behalf, calling the officials' act evil (38:7-9). Zedekiah authorized him to act, and Ebed-Melech took thirty men, gathered old rags and worn-out clothes to cushion the ropes under Jeremiah's arms so they would not cut into him, and carefully drew the prophet up out of the mud (38:10-13) -- a detail of genuine, practical compassion Scripture takes care to record. Afterward, God gave Jeremiah a specific personal word for Ebed-Melech: because he had trusted in the LORD, his life would be spared and he would not fall by the sword when Jerusalem was captured, even amid the citywide catastrophe about to come (39:15-18). Ebed-Melech's brief but vivid account is one of Scripture's clearest illustrations that courageous compassion toward God's servant, even from an outsider with no covenant status of his own, does not go unnoticed or unrewarded by God.

devotionals: Ebed-melech drew Jeremiah up out of the mud of a deadly cistern with careful, costly compassion. Jesus lifts us out of a pit we could never climb ourselves.
Because Ebed-melech trusted the LORD, God promised to spare his life amid coming disaster. Everyone who trusts Jesus is promised that same safety in the judgment to come.
